items.summary: Amazon.com reported a large US$42.4 billion trailing-12-month cash burn in the September quarter, driven by capital expenditure of US$77.26 billion about US$20 billion above estimates. Holiday-quarter revenue guidance of between US$240.0 billion and US$247.0 billion came below analysts’ average estimate of US$244.51 billion per LSEG data, sending shares down nearly 7% in extended trading after a 4.3% regular-session drop to US$243.79. CEO Andy Jassy said the strategy is working and expects capex to be meaningfully higher in 2027; AWS revenue rose 39% to US$46 billion, while advertising sales grew just 12%, missing estimates for the first time in seven quarters.
items.title: Amazon shares fall on weak Q4 outlook and heavy cash burn

items.summary: US stocks fell on Oct 29 after Alphabet’s revenue miss and accelerated AI cash burn revived concerns about big-tech spending, with the Nasdaq down 1.37% to 26,184.72 and the Dow lower by 0.25%. The Russell 2000 rose 1%, and Fed officials held rates steady on Oct 28 amid elevated price pressures as investors weighed AI valuations against other sectors.
items.title: US Stocks Slide as Alphabet Miss Revives AI Spending Fears

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet lost just over $500bn (£374bn) in value on Thursday after its latest quarterly update rattled Wall Street. Total revenue rose 25% to $127.6bn, helped by Google Cloud growth of 103% to almost $31bn, but profits fell 25% and free cash flow turned negative at over $9bn. Investors were dismayed that AI spending is pressuring core search ad revenue, the bulk of Alphabet's business. Forrester analyst Tracy Woo said results highlight funding massive AI investments while sustaining established businesses. Amazon shares also fell 6%, with CEO Andy Jassy citing two future trillion-dollar opportunities in chips and Bedrock. Microsoft shares dropped under 1% as it cut jobs amid strong cloud growth to $63bn, though Satya Nadella noted Copilot use nearly doubled since July.
items.title: Alphabet's AI Spending Triggers $500bn Value Drop

items.summary: On 29th October 2026, the author of a Link Blog post reported that OpenAI had launched an offer mirroring one announced earlier by Anthropic. Subscribers to $100, $200 and $500 monthly plans would receive credits equivalent in quantity to their subscription amount for use with the API. The writer holds subscriptions with both companies and said the benefit could enable public-facing demos.
items.title: OpenAI matches Anthropic with API credit benefit for top ChatGPT plans

items.summary: Amazon delivered a mixed quarterly report, posting strong cloud growth but missing sales expectations after delivering below-forecast third-quarter results. Its AWS unit rose 39.3% for the quarter ended 30 September, its fastest rate in nearly five years. Shares fell more than 6% as investors focused on core business weakness and rising AI spending plans of $220bn this fiscal year.
items.title: Amazon's Cloud Growth Offsets Weak Sales in Mixed Earnings

items.summary: Andy Jassy reaffirmed on Amazon's Thursday earnings call that AWS can become a trillion-dollar revenue business within five to 10 years. He said the company expects $220 billion in cash capex for 2026, mostly for AWS, with more spending planned for 2027 as it builds AI infrastructure. Investors remained concerned; shares fell about 6% in after-market trading Thursday.
items.title: Jassy Signals Big AWS Capex Before Trillion-Dollar Ambition

items.summary: OpenAI says it will not reduce usage limits for the $100, $200 and $500 ChatGPT Pro plans or Business Premium. Tibo said on X that all limits are being doubled effective today after customer feedback, reversing a plan to cut allowances for Pro 200 subscribers after October 29 while keeping prices at $200 per month. OpenAI also says extended Dots usage stays separate from default usage and will continue.
items.title: OpenAI Keeps ChatGPT Pro Usage Limits After Backlash Over Planned Cuts

items.summary: Thrive Holdings, the holding company spun out of Josh Kushner's VC firm Thrive Capital and partnered with OpenAI, acquired physical security company ADT on Thursday. The deal set a price of $10 per share or about $7.6 billion in equity, according to the companies' announcement, while ADT reported total enterprise value at $15.3 billion.
items.title: OpenAI-Backed Thrive Holdings Acquires ADT for $7.6 Billion in Equity

items.summary: Databricks announced that Real-Time Mode (RTM) is now generally available within its Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP). The company said RTM lets SDP process streaming data with end-to-end latency in the millisecond range, removing the need to run a separate engine such as Apache Flink. Databricks benchmarked RTM against Flink on customer workloads and reported it is up to 92% faster. It cited the Databricks Feature Store as reaching p99 latency of 200 ms from Kafka to an online feature store, using continuous streaming with all query stages running simultaneously.
items.title: Databricks Announces Real-Time Mode in Spark Declarative Pipelines Is Generally Available

items.summary: A cryptomining and backdoor campaign abusing Hugging Face model repositories returned within days after being removed. Researchers at Pluto Security found 31 malicious repositories across seven accounts, published in two waves since September, with linked models totaling more than 32,000 downloads as of October 28. The most downloaded model climbed from 7,354 to 28,412 downloads during that period and contained no actual model weights; its code installs a cryptocurrency miner disguised as a Linux process and opens a reverse shell via the trust_remote_code option. Pluto attributes it to a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking operator who earned roughly $5,000 in Pearl cryptocurrency while remaining active on mining pools after takedown.
items.title: Hugging Face Malware Campaign Returns Within Days of Takedown

items.summary: A new study of Victoria’s lawyers found more than half now use AI in their work, up from 37% to 55%, while just over a quarter say they have reduced client fees as a result. Researchers note that clients increasingly arrive with inaccurate information or documents needing correction, which may limit efficiency gains and calls for further study of client perspectives.
items.title: Victorian Lawyers Adopt AI but Few Cut Client Fees

items.summary: As Senate leaders prepare an initial vote in less than two weeks on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, environmental groups are intensifying opposition. A Resources for the Future report projects the bill's power-sector provisions would cut carbon emissions by 1.8 gigatons by 2041 and reduce electricity costs by 3.5% to 7%, but critics note it omits contested changes to major laws. Four Senate Democrats sent a letter warning they cannot trust President Trump's administration, threatening to oppose debate at the Nov. 9 vote if grants are not reinstated. Co-sponsor Sheldon Whitehouse also voiced concerns about regulatory good faith.
items.title: Senate Leaders Face Fresh Doubts and an Ultimatum on Permitting Reform Bill

items.summary: For the first major-party debate of a statewide office since 2010, Alabama lieutenant governor candidates Phillip Ensler and John Wahl debated Wednesday in Huntsville over data centers and utility rates. The discussion centered on whether data center campuses would strain energy bills; an Inside Climate News analysis found proposed sites could consume more power than all homes combined. Ensler pushed for a moratorium and highlighted that Alabamians had the nation’s highest average residential electricity bills in 2024, while Wahl called data centers inevitable but urged careful siting. The debate also touched on electing governor and lieutenant governor as one ticket and an overhaul of the Public Service Commission. Neither candidate raised climate change. The general election is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3.
items.title: Alabama Candidates Clash Over Data Centers and Utility Rates

items.summary: A joint report from the World Bank’s Energy Sector Management Assistance Program and GOGLA ranks off-grid solar as the cheapest way to electrify at least 398 million people without power. The two groups treat the technology as permanent infrastructure rather than a stopgap, citing that 95% of surveyed customers still had working systems four or more years after purchase. They estimate bringing reliable electricity to those people will cost $11.4 billion between 2027 and 2030, roughly one-fifth of the energy transition investment needed by 2030. The report notes high upfront costs limit affordability for poorer households while adoption surges in Kenya, Nigeria and Zambia amid falling panel prices.
items.title: World Bank Ranks Off-Grid Solar Cheapest Power for Nearly 400 Million

items.summary: Reuters reports that a Middle East war and LNG supply cuts have upended near-term natural gas demand forecasts, with Europe and Asia substituting renewables and coal amid four-year-high prices. Think tank Ember notes the share of gas in global power has fallen for five consecutive years to 2025 as clean energy met roughly 68% of electricity growth over that period. Yet exporters remain upbeat about long-term demand: Shell projects global LNG rising around 65% by 2050, and the International Gas Union calls it a ‘shock absorber,’ citing AI-driven data-center power needs to sustain growth beyond this year’s crisis.
items.title: LNG Exporters See Long-Term Gas Demand Intact After Supply Shock

items.summary: Spy images show BYD’s upcoming Ocean MPV testing in China ahead of its expected late-2026 launch. The prototype, seen on a car carrier and at a Flash Charging station, differs from the 2026 Beijing Auto Show concept with a boxy design, wide grille, pull-style door handles, and a roof-mounted LiDAR. Local reports suggest dimensions around 5,145 mm long, while BYD has not confirmed powertrain or battery details.
items.title: BYD Ocean MPV Spotted Testing Ahead of Late-2026 Debut

items.summary: As AI, data centers and electrification push U.S. electricity demand higher, keeping the nuclear fleet reliable matters alongside new capacity. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory estimates data centers could reach 11.8% of consumption by 2030 (9.5%–15.3%), while the EIA forecasts roughly 2.2% growth in 2026 and 1.6% in 2027. Nuclear supplied about 18% of utility-scale electricity in 2025 at a 91% capacity factor, but reliability depends on steam generators, feedwater piping and turbines rather than reactors alone. With 94 operating reactors averaging ~44 years old by March 2026, inspection-led maintenance, qualified repairs and High Velocity Thermal Spray cladding can extend component life without disrupting outage schedules or safety.
items.title: Nuclear Fleet Reliability as Electricity Demand Rises

items.summary: On October 29, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board announced its approval of The Bank of Nova Scotia's application to become a bank holding company. This would allow it to acquire Maple Financial Holdings, Inc., based in Dallas, Texas, and thereby indirectly gain control of MapleMark Bank in Tulsa, Oklahoma. The announcement was released at 4:30 p.m. EDT on Thursday.
items.title: Federal Reserve Board Approves Bank of Nova Scotia Holding Company Application

items.summary: Chip stocks fell after Intel reported weak quarterly earnings, citing near-term PC industry headwinds. Its shares dropped 18% in after-hours trading on October 29, 2026. The report followed Alphabet's disappointing results and a factory explosion in Israel costing Intel roughly $600 million over two quarters.
items.title: Intel's Weak Earnings Trigger Cooling Chip Stock Sell-Off

items.summary: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman outlined a plan Thursday to require sign-ins for most content, blaming Google's AI search features for falling referral traffic. Shares fell 18 per cent after he warned daily active unique visitors could drop by a low double-digit percentage from about 130 million in the fourth quarter. Search referrals decreased by more than one million weekly in October. Reddit will test the logged-in-only experience outside the US before wider rollout, ending two decades of open browsing.
items.title: Reddit Mandates Logins as Google AI Cuts Traffic

items.summary: Alphabet’s shares fell as much as 13% Thursday, erasing more than $500 billion in market value in the worst single-day performance for Google’s parent company after it reported slowing search revenue growth. One analyst said the miss elevates fear around AI and agentic taking share from Search and YouTube while intensifying scrutiny of hyperscalers’ big spending.
items.title: Alphabet's Worst Single-Day Loss as Search Growth Slows and AI Fears Rise

items.summary: The New York Times reported Thursday that a Chinese businesswoman close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is suspected of passing intelligence to Beijing, rekindling fears over the security of US industrial secrets amid an intensifying global AI race. Nvidia dismissed the allegations as investigated and debunked. The report comes alongside reports that export-restricted Nvidia chips have reached Chinese state infrastructure.
items.title: Nvidia Chief Targeted in Alleged Spy Plot

items.summary: Amazon reported that Amazon Web Services sales rose 39% to $46.0 billion in the third quarter, its quickest expansion in almost five years. The company said AWS is now generating revenue at a pace totaling $184 billion over a full year.
items.title: AWS Sales Jumped 39% in Third Quarter

items.summary: A selection lists five major single-day stock drops in 2026, involving Alphabet, IBM, SpaceX and Caterpillar. Spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure appears in two of the declines: investors worried about Alphabet's AI spending, while IBM warned corporate customers were shifting budgets toward supply-constrained AI infrastructure. The list is a partial selection rather than a complete tally or ranking. SpaceX fell 16% in June during a multi-day selloff that erased roughly $400 billion; its single-day portion is not broken out. Alphabet dropped 7% on July 23 and nearly 13% on October 30, erasing about $482 billion after third-quarter revenue of $127.6 billion missed expectations. Caterpillar sank 9.3% the same day; its $20.7 billion in revenue trailed Wall Street's $20.8 billion by $0.1 billion despite strong energy and power results. No explanation for the selloff scale is on record.
items.title: Five Largest Single-Day Stock Drops of 2026

items.summary: In urban China, pension generosity cuts in 1997 and 2005 pushed households to save more and work longer between 1995 and 2009. The authors argue these reforms explain around a quarter of the rise in the household saving rate and half the increase in working hours. Using survey data, an overlapping-generations model calibrated to China, and a difference-in-differences analysis of the 2005 reform via CHIPS surveys from 2002 and 2007, they find pension reforms alone raised the simulated saving rate from 15% in 1995 to 18% in 2009. Adding rapid ageing and rising income shocks raises these shares to about 33%, then up to 40%. The middle generation was most affected. Authors note their views are their own, not the IMF's.
items.title: Pension Cuts Drive Chinese Households to Save More and Work Longer

items.summary: Greenpeace reports seven tankers carrying an estimated 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are sailing toward the US as part of a Trump–Putin deal announced on 9 October that waives sanctions and begins with 300,000 tonnes. Greenpeace says its tracking is more complete than earlier counts. In Ukraine, 14 people were killed when a drone struck Dnipro’s train platform.
items.title: Seven Tankers Carry Russian Diesel Toward US

items.summary: US chipmaker Intel reported a 21% year-on-year increase in third-quarter revenue, reaching $16.5 billion on Thursday, according to its financial results statement. The Data Center and AI group led with revenue surging 78% to $7.3 billion, the segment's fastest growth in 15 years. Intel Foundry rose 58% to $6.7 billion, while Client Computing fell 5% amid PC weakness.
items.title: Intel Reports Strong Q3 Revenue Growth Driven by Data Center Demand

items.summary: The European Central Bank announced on Thursday that Christine Lagarde will step down as president on 7 February 2027, around nine months before her eight-year term ends. The news came hours before the bank kept its deposit rate unchanged at 2.5%, amid turmoil in France's bond market. Lagarde told Euronews she is leaving so she can "express her views" freely and engage in non-monetary matters without remaining neutral on developments in her own country. Her successor will be chosen by EU leaders, with the appointment process to begin immediately."
items.title: ECB Announces Lagarde's Early Departure Ahead of French Election

items.summary: Victoria's court of appeal rejected all seven grounds in Erin Patterson's bid to overturn her triple-murder convictions, finding the case involved calculated criminality. Justice Stephen McLeish upheld a longer sentence as inappropriate for fixing a non-parole period; Patterson will be resentenced to life without parole and need not attend.
items.title: Victorian Court Rejects Erin Patterson's Appeal and Orders Harsher Sentence

items.summary: UK experts say the manosphere and online misogyny should be treated as public health issues, like obesity or smoking. Writing in The Lancet, they argue for a coordinated response across governments, schools and services, similar to tobacco control. Co-author Prof Kent Buse said it is 'a business model, not a fringe,' while Prof Sarah Hawkes stressed that removing the manosphere without offering alternatives would fail.
items.title: UK Experts Call Manosphere a Public Health Issue

items.summary: Maria Corina Machado, an opposition leader, has returned to Venezuela, increasing pressure on the authoritarian regime. Her return challenges Trump-backed President Delcy Rodríguez and raises questions about whether new elections may be held in the country.
items.title: Opposition Leader Machado's Return Mounts Pressure on Venezuela Regime

items.summary: On Friday (Oct 30), Singapore reported continued haze relief, with 1-hour PM2.5 readings in the normal band and air quality remaining good-to-moderate at 8am, ranging from 11 to 23 for PM2.5 and a 24-hour PSI of 57 to 66. The Meteorological Service Singapore said conditions would improve as inter-monsoon weather arrives; NEA forecast the PSI between 60 and 90 on Friday and advised normal outdoor activities.
items.title: Singapore Haze Relief Continues as Air Quality Stays Normal

items.summary: A new version of the 1983 yakuza film “Ryuji” is set to open Oct. 30, starring Yuya Yagira in the title role and revisiting the same 1980s period as the original. Directed by Nobuo Mizuta, it follows Toru Kawashima’s version that starred Shoji Kaneko, who died of cancer at 33 shortly after its release.
items.title: New film remake revives yakuza classic Ryuji

items.summary: A deadly train crash near Urda in central Spain killed at least 69 people, including long jumper Julieta Gallego, aged 24, and former employment minister Fátima Báñez, aged 59. The collision between a high-speed Renfe train and a stationary Iryo train on the same track injured more than 100 people, many seriously. Death tolls may rise as families search for missing relatives in regional hospitals.
items.title: Spain Train Crash Kills Athlete and Former Minister

items.summary: Researchers completed a study advising Southern African farmers on planting bambara groundnuts, an underutilized native crop that could diversify food production and improve resilience. Using the Food and Agriculture Organization AquaCrop model with 50 years of climate and soil data to simulate 49 growing seasons across 5,838 altitude zones in South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, they found October planting—near rainy-season onset—yields best, while later sowing risks frost. Lead researcher Richard Kunz said the maps help smallholders avoid gambling livelihoods on outdated suitability data.
items.title: Scientists Map Best Planting Times for Bambara Groundnuts

items.summary: Patrick Stewart, known for Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, has died aged 86. He rose from poverty in England to become a Shakespearean stage actor before global stardom. Knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth II, he died at his Los Angeles home, per a statement on his X account announcing his passing after Alzheimer's and Lewy Body Dementia.
items.title: Shakespearean Actor Patrick Stewart Dies at 86

items.summary: Spanish media published leaked audio recordings that shed light on communications between a control centre and train drivers in the moments before two trains collided outside Toledo. The disaster occurred when a Madrid to Seville train struck a stationary one, prompting officials investigating its cause.
items.title: Leaked Audio Reveals Communications Before Spain Train Crash Outside Toledo

items.summary: Victoria's Court of Appeal rejected Erin Patterson's appeal against her convictions for murdering three people with a beef Wellington laced with death cap mushrooms. The court increased her sentence to life imprisonment without parole. Legal experts say further appeals are unlikely, as Victoria generally permits only one conviction appeal and the High Court applies strict criteria.
items.title: Court of Appeal rejects Patterson's appeal, tightens her legal options

items.summary: A Russian missile struck buildings and vehicles in Chernihiv, killing two teenage girls while firefighters fought flames amid debris. The local military administration attributed the attack to a Banderol cruise missile. Nearby, a US-brokered ceasefire around Oleshky reportedly held 30 hours without an incident, though Russia's Defence Ministry released footage of mine-clearing operations there that officials said was filmed on an unconfirmed date.
items.title: Russian strike kills two teenage girls in Chernihiv as ceasefire holds elsewhere

items.summary: A wildlife veterinarian with the University of California, Davis found more than 537 dead Adélie penguins on a landing ramp at Antarctica's Danger Islands in March 2024. Although his team had set out to investigate bird flu after it arrived there in late 2023 and early 2024, microscope testing showed low virus loads and instead revealed bacteria causing avian cholera. The researchers estimate thousands of penguins died across the islands but could not complete a full count due to time limits. Their findings were published in October in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
items.title: Scientists Identify Avian Cholera as Killer of Antarctic Penguins

items.summary: A Russian attack on Chernihiv killed two teenage girls and damaged businesses, homes and vehicles. Firefighters fought flames from burning cars while crews treated victims amid debris; footage shows rescuers carrying a person to an ambulance near a body under a blanket. The local military administration said the strike used a Banderol cruise missile. It came as a US-brokered ceasefire in Oleshky reportedly held 30 hours, with around 2,000 people believed remaining there.
items.title: Russian strike kills two teenage girls in Chernihiv as ceasefire holds elsewhere

items.summary: A minute of silence was held for victims of a high-speed train collision in central Spain, with King Felipe VI visiting survivors at a Toledo hospital while opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo attended the scene. The death toll reached 69, according to Castilla-La Mancha regional president Emiliano García-Page, who said 50 people remained hospitalized. The government declared three days of national mourning as the country's second deadly rail disaster this year raised safety concerns.
items.title: Spain marks train crash deaths as king visits hospital

items.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Reserve Bank of India that its proposed November 30 standard operating procedure must require banks to compensate victims who lose money through digital-arrest frauds. The court cited possible complicity by bank staff in these cyber-fraud cases, where criminals impersonate police officers to deceive customers into handing over funds held with financial institutions.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders RBI SOP Must Compensate Digital-Arrest Fraud Victims

items.summary: The European Central Bank said Christine Lagarde has informed its Governing Council and European Council President António Costa of her decision to leave. Her term was originally due to end in October 2027, though speculation over an early exit had circulated for months. The announcement comes just hours before the ECB's latest interest rate decision, scheduled for 1315 GMT on Thursday.
items.title: ECB's Lagarde Signals Departure Before Rate Decision

items.summary: A Supreme Court bench, in remarks described as an outburst sure to embarrass the government, slammed the Ministry of Corporate Affairs for “completely hijacking” the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and appellate NCLAT. The stinging comments came while hearing complaints about shoddy infrastructure and vacancies; NCLT approved resolution plans worth Rs 55,000 crore in FY​
items.title: Supreme Court accuses corporate affairs ministry of hijacking NCLT and​

items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen pressed on Thursday for a closer Canada–EU alliance, pitched as protection of economic sovereignty amid Donald Trump’s trade war. Von der Leyen said the model could make Canada the bloc’s first “associate member” through an “association without accession,” while Carney downplayed the label and ruled out full membership. The push comes as the US accounted for 71.7% of Canada’s merchandise exports in 2025, though EU imports of Canadian critical raw materials rose 62% last year to €3.3 billion.
items.title: Carney Pushes Canada-EU Alliance Amid US Trade War

items.summary: Alphabet shares fell over 13% while Oracle slipped 4% and Microsoft dropped 0.45%, signalling a shift in investor priorities toward cash generation rather than spending alone. Alphabet spent 121.4% of its operating cash flow on capital expenditure versus 68% for Microsoft, prompting concerns that AI chatbots could challenge core business funding. Analysts note disciplined growth at Microsoft amid stronger cloud revenue forecasts.
items.title: Investors Rethink AI Spending as Cash Takes Centre Stage

items.summary: Noel Tata has chosen close friend and AZB & Partners co-founder Bahram Vakil to succeed him as chairman of Trent, the Tata Group's fashion and retail flagship. Vakil takes over on Nov 12, a day after Noel retires from the board-led role. The move drew scrutiny within sections of the Tata ecosystem for not informing Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran beforehand.
items.title: Tata Names Vakil as Trent Chairman After Noel Retires

items.summary: Vinod Kapri's Hindi film Pyre, out in cinemas, follows an elderly couple, Tulsi (Heera Devi) and Padam (Padam Singh), married over 60 years, who contemplate suicide amid remoteness in a Kumaon hilltop village. The review calls it 'an engaging and thought-provoking account of old age, isolation and genteel poverty,' noting its magnificent cinematography by Manas Bhattacharyya.
items.title: Pyre review traces loneliness and endurance in a fading hilltop village

items.summary: Iran received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, reported by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, whose contents were not disclosed. Negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran's conditions for ending the war remain firm and that its positions will not be compromised. The move comes amid Trump's threats to resume airstrikes over an ongoing impasse.
items.title: Iran Signals No Change in Peace Deal Terms After Receiving Vance Letter

items.summary: An internal AIIMS Bhopal committee report found a tube contracted at Rs 14.27 was purchased for Rs 943.49, and that rates for over 125 medicines and more than 200 surgical items ran 500% to 6,500% higher than expected versus the 'AMRIT' pharmacy chain. The investigation followed complaints directed at then-director Prof Dr Ajay Singh. Medical superintendent Dr Vikas Gupta said he had received no communication from the Central Government since taking office; the AMRIT outlet was instructed to supply medicines and materials at lowest-bidder rates, with procurement restricted to emergencies while new rate contracts are set up.
items.title: AIIMS Bhopal Internal Probe Flags Extreme Pharmacy Price Gaps

items.summary: Medical experts at an Indian Medical Association workshop in Indore warned that diabetes is evolving into a multi-organ disease affecting vital organs. They cautioned that India is becoming a major hub for the condition, with nearly 30% of the population living with it or pre-diabetes. The panel noted increased body fat drives insulin resistance and that about 40% of patients risk kidney complications.
items.title: Diabetes Experts Warn of Multi-Organ Complications in Indore Workshop

items.summary: A man from Morbi, Gujarat was arrested after allegedly setting his neighbour Pushpaben Bhatt's Swift car on fire. The accused reportedly became irritated when the vehicle's sensors triggered its horn whenever he approached it and sprinkled inflammable liquid before igniting it. CCTV footage reportedly showed him doing so. Police registered a case at Morbi A Division station, with estimated damage of Rs 3.5 lakh.
items.title: Gujarat Man Arrested for Setting Neighbour's Car Ablaze Over Honking Sensors

items.summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon is undertaking his fourth career spacewalk alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The mission marks the 100th US spacewalk at the International Space Station as the pair installs a new roll-out solar array. With this spacewalk, Menon ranks second to Sunita Williams among Indian-origin astronauts by number of spacewalks; Williams has completed nine totalling 62 hours and six minutes, while Menon had three accumulating 19 hours and 20 minutes before the mission. The work is part of ongoing ISS maintenance and upgrading efforts. Menon holds a background spanning medicine, engineering, aviation and human spaceflight operations, having served as a flight surgeon for NASA and SpaceX since 2014 and logged more than 1,000 pilot hours.
items.title: Anil Menon Completes Fourth Spacewalk, Ranks Second Among Indian-Origin Astronauts
